hypotheses.text: In postnatal PLAA deficiency cohorts, progressive postnatal microcephaly (HP:0000253) and spastic quadriparesis (HP:0002510) have an exact penetrance of 100% (e.g., 7/7 in the Falik Zaccai cohort), whereas prenatal presentations present as lethal structural malformations detectable on fetal ultrasound before progressive microcephaly or spasticity can manifest.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying cohort-specific numerators and denominators across published series is essential for defining core diagnostic criteria versus prenatal presentations, particularly as prenatal exome sequencing uncovers lethal or severe fetal presentations.

evidence.text: Falik Zaccai et al. identified a novel form of leukoencephalopathy in seven patients presenting between ages 2 to 4 months with progressive microcephaly, spastic quadriparesis, and global developmental delay associated with homozygous PLAA p.Leu752Phe mutation.

hypotheses.text: Optic atrophy (HP:0000648) and secondary epileptic seizures (HP:0001250) are variable features of PLAA-related disorder that define a severe PEHO-like (progressive encephalopathy with edema, hypsarrhythmia, and optic atrophy) presentation in a subset of patients rather than obligate findings in 100% of cases.
hypotheses.rationale: Certain cohorts describe PLAA mutations presenting with PEHO syndrome phenotypes including optic atrophy and infantile seizures, but exact frequencies differ across broader leukoencephalopathy and cerebral palsy cohorts.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 19 children evaluated for PEHO and PEHO-like syndrome, one patient was identified with a pathogenic missense variant in PLAA (c.68G>T, p.Gly23Val) presenting with secondary microcephaly, epileptic seizures, and phenotypic overlap with PEHO syndrome.

hypotheses.text: PLAA variants account for approximately 1-2% of atypical or genetic cerebral palsy (CP) cohorts where progressive microcephaly and progressive spasticity mimic complicated dyskinetic or spastic CP.
hypotheses.rationale: Determining the incidence and presentation of PLAA mutations in broad atypical CP cohorts establishes whether the phenotype is regularly misclassified as non-progressive cerebral palsy.

evidence.text: In a study assessing genetic causes of atypical cerebral palsy using exome and genome sequencing, a pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant in PLAA was identified in 1 patient among 10 sequenced atypical CP cases harboring monogenic etiologies.

new_directions.question_text: What is the comprehensive, unified numerator and denominator across all published cohorts (Hall 2017, Falik Zaccai 2017, Chitre 2018, Han 2025) for specific neuroimaging findings such as corpus callosum hypoplasia (HP:0002079) and cerebral/cerebellar atrophy (HP:0002059 / HP:0001272)?
new_directions.rationale: Neuroimaging patterns provide key objective diagnostic criteria to distinguish PLAA mutations from static perinatal encephalopathies and PEHO-like disorders.

new_directions.question_text: What phenotypic differences, if any, exist between homozygous C-terminal mutations (e.g., p.Leu752Phe) and N-terminal missense variants (e.g., p.Gly23Val) regarding seizure severity and survival?
new_directions.rationale: Different variant positions within PLAA's WD40 or ubiquitin-binding domains may modulate severity, explaining why some patients present with PEHO syndrome while others present with leukoencephalopathy.
